stem: The elements in the third period exhibit periodicity in both their chemical and physical properties.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph of the atomic and ionic radii across the third period is shown. 

{{figure:visual_auto_01.png}}

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain the decrease in atomic radius across the third period.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why, for sodium to silicon, the ionic radii are less than the atomic radii.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why, for phosphorus to chlorine, the ionic radii are greater than the atomic radii.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The first ionisation energies of the elements across the third period show a general increase.

Aluminium and sulfur do not follow this general trend.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain why aluminium has a lower first ionisation energy than magnesium.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why sulfur has a lower first ionisation energy than phosphorus.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The elements in the third period, from sodium to silicon, can react with chlorine to form chlorides.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: State and explain the pattern of change of oxidation number which occurs to both chlorine and the different Period 3 elements when they react together.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Give the equations to show the reactions of sodium chloride and silicon(IV) chloride when separately added to water.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Complete the table to describe the structure and bonding in sodium chloride and silicon(IV) chloride.

|  | structure | bonding |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| sodium chloride |  |  |
| silicon(IV) chloride |  |  |
